assumptions: Host-directed correction of the published Periastra; only the roof and the counters change.
Shape intent for the new roof and counters is taken from the five attached reference images; every dimension is taken from the correction brief, which overrides the images.
WCDF gameplay remains unchanged, while miniature cells, the Sun and Moon marks and the reversible king rebate are equipment-expression substitutions; this is not tournament-compliant equipment.
An opened-state render is a held roof pose, not evidence of self-suspension.

build_plan.exit_criteria: All four distinct physical designs pass isolated CAD and visual checks before assembly; all 26 occurrences exported; board and population checks pass; roof fit and exact +100 mm reveal verified; final independent visual review passes.

components.duty: Carry all 24 counters and support the removable roof.
components.form: 190 by 190 by 24 mm rounded square solid-bottom observatory plinth; 3 mm perimeter walls lower to z17 along the open side spans, retaining z24 corner piers beyond coordinates 88 mm; 176 mm checkerboard at z11; 32 dark cells recessed 0.8 mm; two 3 mm radius stellar half-discs raised 0.8 mm outside board. Each recessed-square mouth has1.5 mm corner radius and0.3 mm lower bevel, retaining22 mm pitch and0.8 mm depth; diagonal junctions retain0.879 mm continuous material webs without a raised grid.
components.interfaces: 184 mm square inner opening; four integral 3 by 3 mm corner ledges occupy signed coordinates 89 to 92 mm on both axes, supported from floor z11 to top z21; roof plate 182.4 mm square gives 0.8 mm clearance per side.
components.name: Observatory board base
components.placement: Centered on x=y=0; bottom z=0; floor z=11; board spans -88 to 88 on x and y.

components.duty: Cover and store the full starting position with intentional rim ventilation and partial counter-edge visibility when closed; expose the populated board when lifted 100 mm vertically.
components.form: 182.4 mm square solid backing plate 3 mm thick with 1.2 mm corner rounding and a flat underside, carrying a 180 mm diameter drum 14 mm high; one square-cut rotation-ring seam 2 mm wide and 1 mm deep runs all the way round the drum, centred 4 mm below its top, its upper wall relieved at 50 degrees from vertical so it needs no support. A smooth spherical cap of 90 mm base radius and 40 mm rise (sphere radius 121.25 mm) sits on the drum. One 30 mm wide shutter slit with parallel square-cut walls is cut through both dome and drum on a single meridian in the YZ plane, open from the bottom of the drum, over the apex, and 30 mm of surface run down the far side, so the far half of the cap stays unbroken. A blunt-ended 24 mm diameter tube on a 45 degree axis emerges through the slit, carried on a fork of two 6 mm thick arms that cradle it and rise into prongs clear above it, standing on a solid pier on the plate; pier, arms and tube are one fused buttressed structure fused to both inside walls of the slit. No railing, walkway, ladder, panelling, rib, rivet or window; one single solid.
components.interfaces: Flat underside rests on four base ledges; 0.8 mm lateral play against 184 mm opening; no downward skirt, hinge, latch or hardware.
components.name: Domed observatory roof with shutter slit
components.placement: Closed backing plate bottom z21, top z24; drum z24 to z38; rotation-ring seam centred z34; dome apex z78; telescope highest point z77.0 and fork prong tips z76, both within the 180 mm plan envelope; opened roof is the exact closed solid translated +100 mm Z.

components.duty: One independently movable draughts man or king; the same sunk mark appears on both faces, so its side reads whichever way up it lies.
components.form: Plain round draughts disc, 16.0 mm diameter and 7.0 mm thick, perfectly circular outline with no tail, tab, notch or projection, 1.0 mm chamfer on the man-face edge. The same symbol pocket, 1.2 mm deep with square vertical walls and a flat floor, is sunk into both faces: a 4.4 mm ball dead centre with eight separate rays round it, each widest at its inner end and narrowing to a blunt 1.0 mm flat tip, separated from the ball by a 1.0 mm undisturbed band. Overall mark extent 10.0 mm. The man face carries the mark and nothing else. The king face carries a flat annular rebate 2.0 mm wide and 1.2 mm deep round the edge, leaving a 12.0 mm raised plateau with the same mark sunk into it.
components.interfaces: Fits a 22 mm dark square with 3 mm nominal edge margin; at least 2.0 mm of flat undisturbed band between the mark and the man-face chamfer, and at least 1.0 mm between the mark and the edge of the king-face plateau.
components.name: Sun counter 01
components.placement: Sun side occupies its twelve dark squares in the nearest three rows, counter bottom z10.2; man face up, rebated king face down initially.

concept.interaction: Lift roof 100 mm straight above base, then place roof aside. Move each of single_01 through single_12 (the Sun counters) and forked_01 through forked_12 (the Moon counters) under unchanged English draughts gameplay; turn a counter over to its rebated king face upon promotion. The same Sun or Moon mark is sunk into both faces, so a piece’s owner reads whichever way up it lies. Replace every counter on its starting square and reseat roof on base for storage.
concept.print_stance: Base bottom down; roof flat solid backing plate down with the dome apex up; both counter designs flat with the plain man face down, so the annular king rebate and its plateau print upwards. Four distinct parametric part entries, 26 production occurrences.
risks: CAD checks must establish printability, fit and seated visibility; no physical test is claimed.
3 mm radius border half-discs are deliberately compact to preserve the entire 176 mm playing area and 3 mm walls.
The 0.8 mm clearance is nominal CAD clearance, not measured printed fit.

The undisturbed band between the sun’s ball and its rays is 1.0 mm, and the raised gaps between adjacent rays are about 0.6 mm; both are below the 3 mm minimum feature width the rest of the set observes. They are shallow relief on a solid disc, not standing walls, so they are a legibility risk at a 0.4 mm nozzle rather than a fragility risk.
concept.signature_decision: A domed observatory with an open shutter slit and a telescope on a fork covers and stores a complete populated draughts board, and reveals the playing surface by one exact vertical roof lift. The counter’s king step is the dome’s rotation ring at counter scale.
concept.summary: English draughts — a syzygy: the Sun side and the Moon side meet across the board an observatory dome is built to watch, and the dome tracks them.
concept.title: Periastra Syzygy

design_changes.change: Roof replaced: truncated cone, telescope hood and hood buttress removed; drum, rotation-ring seam, spherical-cap dome, shutter slit and forked telescope added.
design_changes.previous: 180 mm truncated cone rising 45 mm with an 18 mm cylinder hood at 45 degrees on a solid buttress.
design_changes.reason: Host correction: reduced to silhouette the published part read as a cone, and the only telescope cue was an 18 mm stub that read as a chimney.

design_changes.change: Counters replaced: single-tail and forked-tail comet outlines and the 0.6 mm orbit-crown recess removed; both sides become the same plain round disc differing only by the mark sunk into both faces, with an annular king rebate.
design_changes.previous: Comet silhouettes with a reversible 0.6 mm recessed orbit crown and 1.6 mm notches.
design_changes.reason: Host correction: comets were off-theme inside an observatory, the two tails were not reliably distinguishable across a populated board, and the crown was below what a 0.4 mm nozzle resolves.

design_changes.change: Human-facing names changed: single comet -> Sun counter, forked comet -> Moon counter; part_single_comet.step.py -> part_sun_counter.step.py and part_forked_comet.step.py -> part_moon_counter.step.py. The 26 structural part keys are unchanged.
design_changes.reason: The two sides of the set become the Sun and the Moon, the two bodies an observatory tracks.
Host requires a revision title distinct from the published set; a syzygy is the alignment of the Sun and the Moon. The published Periastra is not updated.

design_changes.change: The shutter slit runs 30 mm of surface arc down the far side of the cap, not 30 mm of vertical drop, so the far half of the dome stays unbroken.
design_changes.previous: First build cut the far side down to z27, opening the slit to 89 per cent of the dome radius.
design_changes.reason: An independent blind reader saw the vertical reading as a dome sawn into two lobes and read the whole part as a computer mouse. With the arc reading the same reader read the part, unprompted, as an astronomical observatory dome with its shutter open.

design_changes.change: The two fork arms extend into prongs that rise clear above the telescope tube.
design_changes.previous: The arms stopped at the tube axis and read as a solid buttress.
design_changes.reason: Gives the telescope a visible mount in profile and down the slit meridian; still two arms rising from the solid pier, still fused to the slit walls, still nothing cantilevered.

design_changes.change: The moon crescent is drawn on an 8.0 mm outer circle (7.2 mm bite offset 3.1 mm) instead of 10.0 mm, keeping its 3.5 mm waist and giving blunter 2.17 mm horn tips.
design_changes.previous: A 10.0 mm crescent whose continuous outer arc sat 1.0 mm inside the king plateau edge.
design_changes.reason: At 10.0 mm the crescent and the 2 mm annular rebate are the same 1.2 mm depth separated by a single 1.0 mm ridge, and an independent blind reader could see no crescent at all on the king face - it read as one broken ring round a blank plateau, which defeats the whole point of putting the same mark on both faces. At 8.0 mm the band is 2.0 mm and the mark separates.

research.novelty_assessment: Bounded title, comet/periastron/checkers and nearby portable/space-checkers searches found adjacent products, not proof of worldwide novelty. Claim only an unusual original combination.
research.popularity_assessment: Two independent cited sources corroborate household-scale and enduring recognition.
research.rights_assessment: Traditional public-domain game mechanics; fresh geometry and original rule prose. WCDF document expression is not copied or represented as public domain.
research.source_game: English draughts (American checkers), unrestricted opening; WCDF 2012 section 1 gameplay

sources.claim: WCDF 2012 section 1 is the frozen source for gameplay and adjudication. Original prose and physical expression will not be copied. Tournament dimensions differ from the explicitly requested miniature equipment.
The Strong records induction in 2003 and reports Pressman's estimate of more than 25 million sets sold since 1922, supporting enduring widespread recognition.
Independent Board Game Central describes American/standard checkers as the most commonly played checkers in the United States. Its simplified rules are not used as this product's rules authority.
Traditional checkers adaptation is explicitly designated Public Domain. This corroborates traditional-game lineage; it does not release WCDF document prose.

US Copyright Office distinguishes unprotected ideas, systems and methods from protected expression. Only traditional gameplay mechanics are implemented, with independently authored text and geometry; no claim that WCDF publication is public domain.
NASA describes comet trajectories changing through gravity and ejection by gravitational encounters. Periastra uses these as a spatial metaphor, not a physical orbital simulation.
Nearby printed space-checkers listing; fetched title establishes proximity but no detailed rules/form claims can be made from its empty body.
Designer describes a sliding board retained by a lip. Periastra has a permanent floor and vertically removed conical roof instead.

research.vault_status: Revision of a published toy; no new vault lesson consumed.
